corrected_value.title: Social heuristics shape intuitive cooperation.

decisions.location: Experiment 3 introduction and Method, lines 273-277; Discussion Experiment 3 and General Discussion, lines 303-309, 355-383; References, line 428
decisions.quote:
Considering that Mechanical Turk workers from the United States are experienced, and that the intuitive-cooperation effect interacts with experience, it might be possible that Rand and colleagues
[8]
recent failures to find an intuitive-cooperation effect in Mechanical Turk experiments as well as our failures to find such an effect in Experiment 1 and in Experiments 2a, 2b and 2c are due to the Mechanical Turk population becoming increasingly experienced in playing public good games. In order to test this experience hypothesis of our replication failures, we conducted a third experiment.
Method
Experiment 3 was an exact replication of our Experiment 2c, but we only tested naïve participants.
decisions.reason: 1. Empirical retesting: After Experiments 1 and 2a-2c fail to replicate the baseline intuitive-cooperation effect of Rand, Greene, & Nowak (2012) [1] Study 6, Verkoeijen & Bouwmeester (2014) note (lines 260-271, 355-363) that Rand et al. (2014) [8] documented a decline of the intuitive-cooperation effect among experienced Mechanical Turk workers and conceptually replicated the interaction with experience showing that the intuitive-cooperation effect holds among naïve participants. Verkoeijen & Bouwmeester (2014) then conduct Experiment 3 with naïve Mechanical Turk participants specifically to empirically test this experience hypothesis and compare their naïve-participant results against Rand et al. [1], [8] (lines 273-279, 303-309, 377-383). Under the codebook replication-chain rule, Rand et al. (2014) [8] is directly retested in Experiment 3. 2.
